BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

October 1993 Price Group 1 



Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee, FAD 9 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the 
draft finalized by the Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Of the various spices exported from India, celery seeds AJMODA accounts for a sizable quantity; 
United Kingdom and United States of America being our biggest buyers. Celery seeds are also 
exported to European countries like France, Italy, Netherlands, West Germany as well as to 
Australia and New Zealand. This standard has been formulated to further augment our export 
of celery seeds 

This standard was first issued in 1966. This revision is brought out for upgrading the requirements 
in line with the International Standard ( ISO ) on celery seeds. Requirements for volatile oil 
content have been incorporated. 

This standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 
1954 and the Rules framed thereunder, wherever applicable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )\ 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard.

IS 3797: 1993 



Indian Standard 

SPICES AND CONDIMENTS — CELERY 
SEEDS — SPECIFICATION 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirements for 
cekry seeds ( Apium graveolens L. ). 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No. Title 

1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water ( third 

revision ) 
1797 : 1985 Methods of test for spices and 

condiments ( second revision ) 
13145 : 1993 Spices and condiments — 

Methods of sampling (first 

revision ) 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the follow- 
ing definitions shall apply. 

3.1.1 Extraneous Matter 

It includes dust, dirt, stones, clay particles, 
chaif and stem or straw. 

3.1.2 Damaged Seeds 

Discoloured, shrivelled and immature seeds. 

3.1.3 Foreign Seeds 

Seeds other than those of Apium graveolens L. 



4 GRADES 

4.1 Celery seeds shall be of three grades, namely, 
Special* Good and Fair (see Table 1 ) 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Description 

The celery seeds shall be the dried, ripe fruits 
of Apium graveolens L. The seeds shall be light 
brown to greyish brown in colour. The shape 
of the seeds shall be ovoid to hemispherical, 
their length about 1 to 1*5. mm and width 5 to 
10 mm. The seeds shall have several raised 
streaks running along their longitudinal axis, 
these streaks being lighter than the rest of the 
seeds. 

5.2 Taste and Aroma or Flavour 

The taste and aroma or flavour of celery seeds 
shall be fresh and characteristic of the type and 
variety. The material shall be free from foreign 
taste and aroma or flavour as well as from any 
musty odour. 

5.3 Freedom from Moulds and Insects Attack 

The celery seeds shall be free from visible insect 
and moulds, and shall be practically free from 
dead insects and contamination by rodents, 
visible to the naked eye, corrected, if necessary, 
in any particular case. In case the magnifica- 
tion exceeds X 10, this fact should be stated 
in the test report.

5.4 The grade designations and the requirements 
for each of them shall be as given in Table 1 . 

6 PACKING 

Celery seeds shall be packed in sound, clean 
and dry containers made of a material which 
shall protect celery seeds from insect infestation 
as well as from any offensive odour. 

7 MARKING 

7.1 The following particulars shall be marked 
or labelled on each container: 

a) Name of the material and grade 

designation, 

b) Variety or trade name, 

c) Batch or code number, 



d) Net mass, 

e) Date of packing, and 

f) Country of origin. 

8 SAMPLING 

8.1 Representative samples of celery seeds shall 
be drawn according to IS 13145 : 1991. 

9 TESTS 

9.1 Tests shall be carried out in accordance 
with Table 1 .
